summary: Episode 097 has two complementary creative histories. The first belongs to The Dark Dick, an anonymous fan artist who watched DVDASA on YouTube, remembered callbacks, produced drawings within two or three hours, sometimes drew live during the show, and described anonymity as the source of the persona's power. The cast treated each next-day image like a gift. That makes fan work a primary archive object—not decoration—and establishes a strict design rule: pseudonym, work, episode, callback and timestamp may be connected, while identity speculation must never become metadata. The second history is Steven Yeun's path from Korea and Troy, Michigan through Kalamazoo College, Chicago improv, The Second City and a late-2009 move to Los Angeles. He describes using John Cho's earlier work as evidence that the opportunity set for Asian American actors was widening; the host's attempt to turn that precedent into rivalry is retained but distinguished from Yeun's own account. Yeun recounts Sharon Bialy requiring a stronger audition before sending him to Frank Darabont, then describes the value of being held to a real standard rather than patronized. His craft plan is sequential: improve acting now, then develop writing, directing and producing. His account of sudden fame centers on lost ordinary freedom, panic and being treated as a collectible spectacle. His most important representation observation is longitudinal: audience language moved from a racial slur, to 'the Asian guy,' to Glenn, to Steven Yeun's own name. The archive preserves that testimony while preventing the slur from becoming an out-of-context discovery label. A brief Daniel Wu appearance bridges directly to Episode 098 and to the Hollywood–China market conversation. The sexualized interrogation, racial hierarchy and racial pseudoscience remain source ideas with warnings and factual annotations rather than being erased; the public layer restricts private relationship material, explicit co-star details and an infant's identity. Named dialogue remains withheld.
